A1.justification: Both PDFs present KAN-AD, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. v1 Appendix C matches v2 Section 4.6; Appendices A and B are retained, supporting a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, inference timings, sensitivity analyses, ablations, and training-contamination experiments in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, inference timings, sensitivity analyses, ablations, and training-contamination experiments in Section 4.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same Fourier and index-based trigonometric functions, first-order differencing, convolutional coefficient estimation, residual connection, dimensional reduction, and linear prediction. Rewritten motivations and simplified equations do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both evaluate KPI, TODS, WSD, and UCR, including the same UCR case study and localized spike/peak-and-drop contamination scenario. The revised description of synthetic-data construction does not establish a distinct task, population, or input condition.

E2.justification: SAND and SubLOF are added to the efficiency comparison in v2 Table 3, having been absent from v1 Table 4. The main accuracy comparator set is unchanged; AT and AnoTrans both denote Anomaly Transformer.

E3.justification: For robustness testing, v1 Section 4.6 describes selecting TODS spike-anomaly samples, whereas v2 Section 4.5 describes synthesizing peak-and-drop datasets following TODS generation methodology. This revises the reported construction procedure without establishing a rerun. Benchmark splits, training budgets, inference batch size, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The CTE, function-family and function-combination ablations, hyperparameter sweep, contamination curves, and UCR case study retain the same questions and displayed evidence. Appendix C and its Table 5 move into v2 Section 4.6; this is not an added ablation.

E5.justification: Both versions report five independent trials with different random seeds and retain the same mean-and-standard-deviation reporting for KAN-AD. No additional uncertainty-estimation procedure or increased run count is reported.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports CPU inference times of 5637 seconds for SAND and 299 seconds for SubLOF. The main accuracy table, existing efficiency entries, and function-combination ablation values are unchanged. Revised headline percentages therefore do not demonstrate improved measured KAN-AD performance.

T1.justification: v2 Sections 1 and 3.2 add the quantitative assertion that an N-term Fourier expansion cannot model periods below 1/N, replacing v1's inverse-FFT motivation for periodic enhancement. This assertion is not proved; the representation theorem and computational equations otherwise remain essentially unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claim of robust, efficient Fourier-based anomaly detection remains. v2 drops the claim of first introducing the Kolmogorov-Arnold theorem to TSAD and reframes headline efficiency from 55-fold acceleration against SOTA to 50% faster inference and 80% fewer parameters against vanilla KAN.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive discussion of filtering difficulties, dual-model computational costs, and VAE underfitting. Periodic enhancement is now explained as compensating for truncated Fourier representation limits. The Chebyshev/MSE explanation is also qualified from a definite conflict to a potential conflict.

D1.justification: v2's introduction newly states that KAN-AD code is publicly available and supplies a repository link; v1 contains no corresponding access information. This improves documented access without establishing the repository's contents or availability from the PDFs alone.

R1.justification: v2 adds Siffer et al. (2017), removes background references including KAN 2.0 and Braun and Griebel, and strengthens discussion of VAE limitations. Its SAND description changes to shape-based clustering, consistent with the retained Appendix B. The principal TSAD/KAN research context remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, substantial method explanations, and related-work discussion are extensively rewritten or condensed. Architecture and function representation are merged, experimental settings are regrouped, and the function-deconstruction ablation moves from Appendix C into the main evaluation.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted from ACM to ICML styling, changing front matter, typography, headers, captions, and appendix column layout. The function table and ablation table are relocated, and the efficiency table gains two rows. Existing figure graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: New code-access information, less repetitive method explanations, and placing the existing function-deconstruction ablation within the evaluation modestly improve usability and reproducibility documentation. Scientific evidence remains largely unchanged. These gains are partly offset by a new inconsistency: v2 includes SAND and SubLOF timings while its accompanying text still says those methods were excluded.
